data.description: Amended and expanded CCPA, effective 2023. Added right to correct and right to limit sensitive data use.
data.notes: Passed as ballot initiative (Proposition 24) in November 2020, operative January 2023. Created the California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA) as a dedicated enforcement body. Added new consumer rights: right to correct inaccurate information, right to limit use of sensitive personal information. Introduced data minimization requirements and expanded opt-out rights.

data.description: Requires websites collecting personal information from California consumers to post a privacy policy. Effective 2004.
data.notes: One of the first US privacy laws. Requires conspicuous privacy policy, disclosure of categories of personal information collected, and description of the process for notifying consumers of changes. Predates CCPA by over 15 years. Enforced by the California Attorney General.

match_nodes.description: California SB 243 — Companion Chatbots (Business and Professions Code § 22600 et seq.)

data.official_name: California Senate Bill 243 — Companion Chatbots (Chapter 22.6, Division 8, Business and Professions Code, § 22600 et seq.)
alternate_names: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 22600 et seq.
data.description: California statute regulating companion chatbot platforms: requires clear and conspicuous AI disclosure if a reasonable person could be misled into believing they are interacting with a human, recurring 3-hour AI notifications and sexually explicit content blocks for known minor users, suicidal-ideation/self-harm prevention protocols with crisis hotline referrals, annual metrics reporting to the Office of Suicide Prevention (beginning July 1, 2027), and a private right of action ($1,000 minimum statutory damages per violation).
data.notes: Status: In force January 1, 2026 (signed by Governor Newsom October 13, 2025; Chapter 677, Statutes of 2025; verified as of 2026-11-03).

data.note: Extracted statutory section identifiers in dataset-public-laws-regulations-standards (regulation/ca.gov/sb-243).

match_nodes.description: California SB 1119 — Adam's Law (Companion Chatbot Child Safety)

data.official_name: California Senate Bill 1119 — Adam's Law (Companion Chatbots: Child Safety and Risk Assessments)
data.description: California follow-on companion chatbot child-safety legislation expanding SB 243 with mandatory pre-deployment child-safety risk assessments, age assurance, default minor-protection settings, mandatory 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline integration, and biennial independent third-party safety audits.
data.notes: Status: Enacted in 2026; operative provisions phase in during 2027 (introduced February 2026 in the 2025-2026 California Regular Session; verified as of 2026-11-03).

match_nodes.description: California SB 1120 — Physicians Make Decisions Act

data.official_name: California SB-1120: Physicians Make Decisions Act (Health & Safety Code § 1367.01; Insurance Code § 10123.135)
data.description: Requires health care service plans and disability insurers using artificial intelligence or algorithmic decision tools for utilization review to ensure medical necessity determinations are made by licensed physicians or health care professionals.
data.notes: Status: Enacted (Approved by Governor September 28, 2024; Chapter 879, Statutes of 2024; effective January 1, 2025; verified as of 2026-11-10).

match_nodes.description: California SB 1001 — Bolstering Online Transparency Act (Bot Disclosure)

data.official_name: Bolstering Online Transparency Act (California Business and Professions Code §§ 17940–17943)
data.description: Prohibits using an automated online account (bot) to communicate or interact with another person in California online with the intent to mislead about its artificial identity for commercial transactions or election influence.
data.notes: Status: Enacted (Approved by Governor September 28, 2018; Chapter 892, Statutes of 2018; effective July 1, 2019; verified as of 2026-11-10).

match_nodes.description: California SB 327 — Information Privacy: Connected Devices

data.official_name: California SB-327: Information Privacy: Connected Devices (Civil Code §§ 1798.91.04–1798.91.06)
data.description: Requires manufacturers of connected devices sold or offered for sale in California to equip devices with reasonable security features appropriate to the nature and function of the device, including unique preprogrammed passwords or first-use password generation.
data.notes: Status: Enacted (Approved by Governor September 28, 2018; Chapter 886, Statutes of 2018; effective January 1, 2020; verified as of 2026-11-10).
